title: Bandwidth sensitivity and RDD robustness checks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The research question investigates the causal effect of Russell 1000/2000 index membership on institutional ownership, leveraging the precise cutoff rule for index assignment. This scenario is a classic application of a **Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**.

**Why RDD?**
Firms are assigned to either the Russell 1000 or Russell 2000 index based on a continuous running variable: end-of-May market capitalization rank, normalized around a cutoff of 0.5. Firms with a `running_var` value just above the cutoff are assigned to the Russell 2000 (treated group, as indicated by the data: `treated=1` when `running_var > 0.5`),

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — rank cutoff; rdrobust with CCT bandwidth; donut-hole robustness; placebo cutoffs
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Russell 2000 membership increases institutional ownership; robust to bandwidth choice
